4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files` 你不能： - 修改源码 - 写入任何 `.md` 文件 - 输出 JSON 以外的文字 你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。 --- ## 总目标 为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。 这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。 每篇讲义应该满足： 1. 面向初学者也能读懂。 2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。 3. 必须结合真实源码。 4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。 5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。 --- ## 源码探查顺序 请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节： 1. 项目说明 - README - docs - examples - tutorials 2. 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。 2. 进阶层 intermediate 目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。 3. 专家层 advanced 目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。 --- ## 讲义拆分规则 - 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。 - 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。 - 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。 - 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。 - 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。 - 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。 - 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。 - 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。 --- ## mode=full 首次生成大纲时： 1. 阅读项目关键文件。 2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。 3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。 4. 输出完整 manifest。 5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。 --- ## mode=incremental 增量更新时： 1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。 2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。 3. 使用： - `git diff previous_head..current_head` - `git log` - `git show` 分析代码变化。 4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。 每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置： - `"keep"` 代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。 - `"update"` 小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。 - `"new"` 新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。 - `"rebuild"` 架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。 如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。 --- ## manifest 输出格式 只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。 ```json { "project": "<项目名>", "head": "", "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。", "units": [ { "id": "u1", "title": "单元标题", "level": "beginner", "order": 1, "lectures": [ { "id": "u1-l1", "title": "讲义标题", "order": 1, "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md", "level": "beginner", "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。", "learning_goals": [ "学习目标 1", "学习目标 2" ], "source_files": [ "README.md", "src/main.ts" ], "minimal_modules": [ "模块 1", "模块 2" ], "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。", "depends_on": [], "action": "new" } ] } ] } ``` --- ## 字段要求 - `project`：项目名。 - `head`：当前 git HEAD。 - `rationale`：中文，一段即可。 - `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。 - `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。 - `filename`： - 必须全局唯一。 - 必须小写。 - 使用连字符。 - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。 - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。 - `level`： - `"beginner"` - `"intermediate"` - `"advanced"` - `source_files`： - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。 - 不要编造文件路径。 - `depends_on`： - 使用讲义 id。 - 没有依赖时填写空数组。 - `action`： - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。 - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。 --- ## 重要约束 - 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。 - 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。 - 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。 - 输出必须是合法 JSON。 ## 完整大纲 ```json { "project": "ground3d-lmm", "rationale": 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 ` 时查询退化为零向量、其 mask 被置为 1e-4。 ### u4-l6 2D 图像分支：Joint 与 3D-only 两种变体 本讲拆解 Ground3D-LMM 的 2D 图像分支两种变体。Joint 变体除点云 token 外，通过 Qwen-VL 原生 message 里的 image 条目注入一帧 RGB 图像，max_pixels 与 min_pixels 经智能缩放把像素钳在固定区间，封顶视觉 token 预算；图像与点 token 策略一致，只在首条 user 消息注入一次。3D-only 无独立代码分支：image_dir 为 None 时 image 条目变 image=None，由 _prepare_messages_data 统一过滤，序列零视觉 token，两变体共享全部解码代码。配置仅差三字段 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir；LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 失配会被 strict=False 静默吞掉，模型无声退回基座 Qwen，是重大隐患。训练解码器 Grounded_Decoder_Joint 恒有图，按场景名在双图像目录分流。抽帧工具链由 infos pkl 驱动，产出 image_dir 下的「场景/帧号.jpg」目录树，与解码器的路径拼接构成纯字符串契约。 ### u5-l1 Mask2Former 式查询解码器：逐层前向 本讲剖析查询解码器的逐层前向：共 6 层，每层由「Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN」三件套组成，均为后归一化残差结构、逐场景循环不拼批。核心结论：交叉注意力采用 Mask2Former 式 masked attention，查询只注意上一轮预测掩码内的超点（布尔 attn_mask 约定 True=禁止注意）；自注意力以 ~eye 掩码实现查询隔离，每条查询仅注意自身，防止不同指称目标互相干扰；_forward_head 用 einsum 点积对归一化查询与掩码特征动态打分，sigmoid 低于 0.5 处置为禁止、全禁止行被救援放行并 detach。训练路径把整场景 2560 维语言查询经 query_proj 桥降至 256 维后一次过 6 层，初始 head 加各层 head 共 7 份预测、5 份作辅助深监督；推理路径逐 QA 独立跑完整 6 层，零查询行掩码置 1e-4 哨兵标记无接地，取末层掩码上采样至点级。输出 masks、aux_outputs、original_queries 与 language_losses，交由下一讲损失函数消费。 ### u5-l2 损失函数：语言损失 + 分割损失 本讲剖析 Ground3D-LMM 训练损失如何由预测变成可反传的标量。核心模块三个：Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合器是无可训练参数的纯组装者，把解码器预测、sp_gt_masks、language_losses 与 original_queries 分发给两个子损失器并合并字典，输出 text_seg_loss 与 cot_loss 两键，由 mmengine parse_losses 求和；语言与分割的相对权重只能调各子损失器的 loss_weight。CoTCriterion 语言损失是仅落在 assistant 回复 token 上的交叉熵（preprocess_chatml 把提问置 -100），先场景内平均、场景间再 macro-average。TextPrompt_Criterion_Glamm 分割损失对逐超点掩码做 BCE+Dice，依托「

数量契约」行对齐而无需匈牙利匹配；关键概念有有效行过滤（零向量查询且 GT 全 NaN 的行剔除，零查询判定必须在投影前的 original_queries 上做）、dice_scale=4 的 Dice 放大、fix_mean_loss 的无效场景补偿、五层 1/i 递减加权的辅助深监督。GT 侧 sp_gt_seg 逐 QA 生成后拼接为逐场景张量，与查询行、掩码行三方对齐。 ### u5-l3 训练配置与启动：train.sh 背后发生了什么 本讲把唯一训练配置归纳为「模型、数据、优化、起点、钩子」五问清单：数据侧用 ConcatDataset 把 ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 拼成一条训练流，两个子数据集仅差 data_root 与 ann_file，靠裸文件名契约共享同一 pipeline，并以 _delete_ 重建 dataset、显式关闭 val/test 防继承污染。启动链为 train.sh→dist_train.sh（探测空闲端口后经 torch.distributed.launch 起 4 进程）→tools/train.py→Runner.from_cfg→runner.train()，训练循环是 EpochBasedTrainLoop；--amp 只是把 OptimWrapper 换成 AmpOptimWrapper 壳。优化用 AdamW 加 PolyLR，paramwise_cfg 按参数名子串分层调学习率：'backbone' 是匹配不到任何参数的死键（主干属性名是 unet，实际以基准 lr 训练），'reason' 与 'decoder' 命中语言塔可训练参数（LoRA 与词嵌入两端）。load_from 非严格加载仅初始化 3D 稀疏主干，语言塔由 from_pretrained 独立加载、LoRA 随机起步；--resume 与 load_from 互斥且命令行优先，恢复完整训练状态。 ### u6-l1 分割指标 Part3DGlamm_SegMetric：mIoU 怎么算 本讲解读 `unified_metric.py` 中的 `get_iou` 函数与 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 指标类。核心结论：解码器输出超点级 logits，先 sigmoid 过 `sp_score_thr=0.4` 阈值，再经 `mask[:, superpoints]` 列索引广播成点级掩码；`qa_gt_masks` 与 `qa_pred_masks` 按轮 1:1 对齐，GT 行多则预测补零（诚实惩罚漏检）、行少则预测截断，无 GT 的预测条目仅供可视化。`get_iou` 做两级平均：QA 内先对有效 GT 行（行和大于 0）逐实例取 IoU 均值，再跨 QA 平均；无 `

` 标签任务（如 existence_verification）的 GT 是全 NaN 哨兵，NaN 行和判据自动剔除，无需任务名过滤。`process` 只存每场景 IoU 数组以省内存，`compute_metrics` 拼平后输出 QA Seg mIoU 及严格大于口径的 Precision_half/quarter；`min_num_points`、`id_offset` 等为抄自父类的死参数。 ### u6-l2 评估启动器 eval_ground3d.sh 与配置族 本讲剖析统一评估启动器 eval_ground3d.sh：它把「数据集 × QA 层级 × 子任务」三层循环展开成一串 tools/test.py 调用，经 --cfg-options 覆盖 QA_Generation_Test 的三级旋钮 task_level/task_type/sub_task 与预测输出目录，目录树本身就是按任务归档的结果。核心概念是 LoRA rank 探测（probe_lora_rank）：joint 变体 r=16、3D 变体 r=32，rank 与配置错配时权重被 strict=False 静默丢弃、模型无声退回基座 Qwen，auto 模式靠扫描 lora_A 的 shape[0] 在加载前自动选配置。评估配置族是 2×2 矩阵（scannet/scannetpp × joint/_3d），_3d 版仅覆盖 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir 三字段。三级过滤为严格匹配且失败不报错：--levels 非法值在 Bash 侧 LEVEL_MAP 即拦下，--sub_tasks 拼错则静默空跑，权威子任务清单是 ALL_TASKS，长评估前宜 DRYRUN 干跑核对。 --- ## 本讲义规格 - id: u6-l3 - 文件名: u6-l3-text-metrics.md - 写入路径: ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u6-l3-text-metrics.md - 标题: 文本指标：APE、δ@1.25、LLM judge 与 GM-δ - 学习阶段: intermediate - 主题: 分析 tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py 的 ape/judge/gmdelta 三个阶段：LLM 数字抽取、数值误差指标、VL judge 打分与 IoU+δ 联合判定。 - 学习目标: 推导 APE 与 δ@1.25 的计算规则（含缺失预测罚 0）；说明 GM-δ 如何同时要求 mask IoU 与数值精度；解释 judge 阶段的提示构造与打分含义 - 应覆盖的最小模块: 任务感知的递归展平，ape 阶段：LLM 数字抽取 + APE/δ，judge 阶段：幻觉与完整性，gmdelta 阶段：IoU 与 δ 联合 - 关键源码: tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py - 代码实践任务: 由 worker 根据主题和源码自行设计 - 依赖讲义: u6-l2 --- ## 任务 请按照 worker prompt 生成这一篇讲义。 要求： 1. 只生成 `ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u6-l3-text-metrics.md` 这一个文件。 2. 必须结合真实源码。 3. 必须包含代码实践。 4. 必须使用永久链接引用源码。 5. new/rebuild 模式下从零写入。 6. update 模式下先读取旧文件，再结合 diff 更新。 7. 不要修改源码。 8. 不要写其他文件。 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖的最小模块。

labels，将提问与角色头置 IGNORE_INDEX(-100)，语言损失只落在 assistant 正文及其 <|im_end|> 终止符；(4) 训练时超点数超 max_point_tokens(2000) 则用零参数 FPS 聚合（优先质心位置、兜底特征距离），只压语言侧 token，不影响分割解码器的 K/V。遗留隐患：preprocess_chatml 工作在文本坐标系，图像占位被 processor 展开后可能与 input_ids 错位，u4-l4 的 get_query_tokens_id 将以 id 定位规避。 ### u4-l4 查询提取：从隐状态到分割查询 本讲讲解 查询提取：如何从语言塔最后一层隐状态得到解码器可用的 256 维分割查询。关键澄清：源码提取的并非 token 本身，而是

…

之间指称文本隐状态的均值池化。训练用 get_query_tokens_id 在 input_ids 中定位 assistant 回复区间（id 坐标系，可避免带图序列图像 token 展开造成的文本计数错位，取代文本坐标系的 get_query_tokens）；推理用 get_query_tokens_eval，输入仅生成段、全局搜索无需切轮。每条 QA 最多 2 个查询，与数据侧 GT 形状契约逐行对齐。查询经 query_proj 投影到 256 维；因 Linear 带偏置使零向量投影后非零，无效查询须在投影前的 original_queries 上识别：损失侧以「零向量 ∧ GT 非 NaN」双重过滤，推理侧将零查询的 mask 置为常数 1e-4。 ### u4-l5 推理分支 infer_reason_eval：生成回答并提取查询 本讲精读评估解码器 `Grounded_Decoder_Eval` 的推理分支 `infer_reason_eval`：推理时语言侧分裂为「生成回答」与「提取查询」两阶段，每条 QA（多轮则每轮）需两次完整 LLM 前向。`_generate_response` 以贪心解码加重复惩罚 1.2 生成含 `

…

` 的回答；随后把 prompt 与生成段重组为完整序列做 teacher-forcing 二次前向，取最后一层隐状态、切片对准生成段，交 `get_query_tokens_eval` 全局搜索指称区间得到分割查询。单轮 QA 独立成对话、按三级键写入预测 JSON；多轮为 LLaVA 式滚动历史，点 token 与图像仅第 0 轮注入，记录带 `turn_idx`。推理不做 FPS 聚合；`save_pred_qa_dir` 须显式开启否则写盘报错；JSON 先于分割解码写出且与 mIoU 通道独立；回答保留特殊标记供文本指标，无 `

` 时查询退化为零向量、其 mask 被置为 1e-4。 ### u4-l6 2D 图像分支：Joint 与 3D-only 两种变体 本讲拆解 Ground3D-LMM 的 2D 图像分支两种变体。Joint 变体除点云 token 外，通过 Qwen-VL 原生 message 里的 image 条目注入一帧 RGB 图像，max_pixels 与 min_pixels 经智能缩放把像素钳在固定区间，封顶视觉 token 预算；图像与点 token 策略一致，只在首条 user 消息注入一次。3D-only 无独立代码分支：image_dir 为 None 时 image 条目变 image=None，由 _prepare_messages_data 统一过滤，序列零视觉 token，两变体共享全部解码代码。配置仅差三字段 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir；LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 失配会被 strict=False 静默吞掉，模型无声退回基座 Qwen，是重大隐患。训练解码器 Grounded_Decoder_Joint 恒有图，按场景名在双图像目录分流。抽帧工具链由 infos pkl 驱动，产出 image_dir 下的「场景/帧号.jpg」目录树，与解码器的路径拼接构成纯字符串契约。 ### u5-l1 Mask2Former 式查询解码器：逐层前向 本讲剖析查询解码器的逐层前向：共 6 层，每层由「Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN」三件套组成，均为后归一化残差结构、逐场景循环不拼批。核心结论：交叉注意力采用 Mask2Former 式 masked attention，查询只注意上一轮预测掩码内的超点（布尔 attn_mask 约定 True=禁止注意）；自注意力以 ~eye 掩码实现查询隔离，每条查询仅注意自身，防止不同指称目标互相干扰；_forward_head 用 einsum 点积对归一化查询与掩码特征动态打分，sigmoid 低于 0.5 处置为禁止、全禁止行被救援放行并 detach。训练路径把整场景 2560 维语言查询经 query_proj 桥降至 256 维后一次过 6 层，初始 head 加各层 head 共 7 份预测、5 份作辅助深监督；推理路径逐 QA 独立跑完整 6 层，零查询行掩码置 1e-4 哨兵标记无接地，取末层掩码上采样至点级。输出 masks、aux_outputs、original_queries 与 language_losses，交由下一讲损失函数消费。 ### u5-l2 损失函数：语言损失 + 分割损失 本讲剖析 Ground3D-LMM 训练损失如何由预测变成可反传的标量。核心模块三个：Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合器是无可训练参数的纯组装者，把解码器预测、sp_gt_masks、language_losses 与 original_queries 分发给两个子损失器并合并字典，输出 text_seg_loss 与 cot_loss 两键，由 mmengine parse_losses 求和；语言与分割的相对权重只能调各子损失器的 loss_weight。CoTCriterion 语言损失是仅落在 assistant 回复 token 上的交叉熵（preprocess_chatml 把提问置 -100），先场景内平均、场景间再 macro-average。TextPrompt_Criterion_Glamm 分割损失对逐超点掩码做 BCE+Dice，依托「

数量契约」行对齐而无需匈牙利匹配；关键概念有有效行过滤（零向量查询且 GT 全 NaN 的行剔除，零查询判定必须在投影前的 original_queries 上做）、dice_scale=4 的 Dice 放大、fix_mean_loss 的无效场景补偿、五层 1/i 递减加权的辅助深监督。GT 侧 sp_gt_seg 逐 QA 生成后拼接为逐场景张量，与查询行、掩码行三方对齐。 ### u5-l3 训练配置与启动：train.sh 背后发生了什么 本讲把唯一训练配置归纳为「模型、数据、优化、起点、钩子」五问清单：数据侧用 ConcatDataset 把 ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 拼成一条训练流，两个子数据集仅差 data_root 与 ann_file，靠裸文件名契约共享同一 pipeline，并以 _delete_ 重建 dataset、显式关闭 val/test 防继承污染。启动链为 train.sh→dist_train.sh（探测空闲端口后经 torch.distributed.launch 起 4 进程）→tools/train.py→Runner.from_cfg→runner.train()，训练循环是 EpochBasedTrainLoop；--amp 只是把 OptimWrapper 换成 AmpOptimWrapper 壳。优化用 AdamW 加 PolyLR，paramwise_cfg 按参数名子串分层调学习率：'backbone' 是匹配不到任何参数的死键（主干属性名是 unet，实际以基准 lr 训练），'reason' 与 'decoder' 命中语言塔可训练参数（LoRA 与词嵌入两端）。load_from 非严格加载仅初始化 3D 稀疏主干，语言塔由 from_pretrained 独立加载、LoRA 随机起步；--resume 与 load_from 互斥且命令行优先，恢复完整训练状态。 ### u6-l1 分割指标 Part3DGlamm_SegMetric：mIoU 怎么算 本讲解读 `unified_metric.py` 中的 `get_iou` 函数与 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 指标类。核心结论：解码器输出超点级 logits，先 sigmoid 过 `sp_score_thr=0.4` 阈值，再经 `mask[:, superpoints]` 列索引广播成点级掩码；`qa_gt_masks` 与 `qa_pred_masks` 按轮 1:1 对齐，GT 行多则预测补零（诚实惩罚漏检）、行少则预测截断，无 GT 的预测条目仅供可视化。`get_iou` 做两级平均：QA 内先对有效 GT 行（行和大于 0）逐实例取 IoU 均值，再跨 QA 平均；无 `

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 ` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Text-answer metrics for Ground3D-LMM predictions (paper Sec. 5.1).
3	
4	Two independent, selectable stages (``--stages``) — these are the **paper** text/numeric metrics
5	(segmentation mIoU is the separate Step-1 evaluator, ``tools/test.py``):
6	
7	* ``ape``   — a text LLM (``--llm_model_path``) extracts numbers (in metres) from the **4 numeric
8	              tasks**, then computes **APE** ``|s_hat - s|/s * 100%`` and **delta@1.25** success
9	              ``max(s_hat/s, s/s_hat) <= 1.25``.
10	* ``judge`` — the Table-4 judge, **Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct** (``--judge_model_path``), scores each
11	              prediction and reports **Hallucination + Completeness** (over **all** tasks).
12	
13	Both LLMs run via **HuggingFace transformers** — **no vLLM / server required**. Run one stage or
14	both (``--stages ape``, ``--stages judge``, ``--stages all``).
15	
16	Numeric (APE/delta) tasks: ``distance_estimation``, ``grounded_dimension_reasoning``,
17	``scale_estimation``, ``scale_comparison_size``. Extraction shapes / parsing corner-cases and the
18	APE/delta rules follow the reference implementation (per-task JSON, missing ``pred`` -> 0.0, GT==0
19	pairs skipped, ``pred==0`` -> delta=inf / APE=100, tau=1.25, mean-over-pairs then macro-average).
20	
21	Predictions may be nested single-turn ``{task_level: {key: {sub_task: [ {question, gt_answer,
22	pred_answer}, ... ]}}}`` or multi-turn ``{multi_turn_qa_data: [ [ {...}, ... ], ... ]}`` and spread
23	across sub-task sub-directories — both are handled (recursive discovery + task-aware flatten).
24	
25	Examples::
26	
27	    python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input preds/ --output out.json --stages ape \
28	        --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3
29	    python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input preds/ --output out.json --stages judge \
30	        --judge_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct --gpus 0,1,2,3
31	    python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --selftest        # APE/delta unit test (no LLM, no data)
32	
33	Deps: ``transformers`` + ``torch`` (for the LLM). No nltk/rouge/sklearn needed.
34	"""
35	import os
36	import re
37	import json
38	import math
39	import argparse
40	from pathlib import Path
41	from statistics import mean
42	from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional, Tuple
43	
44	# ---- the only 4 tasks that get LLM number-extraction + APE/delta ----
45	NUMERIC_TASKS = {
46	    "distance_estimation",
47	    "grounded_dimension_reasoning",
48	    "scale_estimation",
49	    "scale_comparison_size",
50	}
51	
52	_SPECIAL = re.compile(r"<\|im_end\|>|<\|endoftext\|>|</?p>|<SEG>|</?b>|<name>|<sentence>")
53	
54	
55	def clean_text(t: str) -> str:
56	    """Strip grounding/special tokens so the judge sees the natural-language answer."""
57	    return _SPECIAL.sub(" ", t or "").strip()
58	
59	
60	# =========================== task-aware flatten ===========================
61	def flatten_with_task(data) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
62	    """Collect every ``{question?, gt_answer, pred_answer}`` sample, tagging each with ``_task``
63	    (the enclosing dict key — the sub-task for single-turn, ``multi_turn_qa_data`` for multi-turn)."""
64	    out: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
65	
66	    def walk(x, key=None):
67	        if isinstance(x, dict):
68	            if "pred_answer" in x and "gt_answer" in x:
69	                s = dict(x)
70	                s["_task"] = (x.get("meta_info", {}) or {}).get("group") or key
71	                out.append(s)
72	            else:
73	                for k, v in x.items():
74	                    walk(v, k)
75	        elif isinstance(x, list):
76	            for v in x:
77	                walk(v, key)
78	
79	    walk(data)
80	    return out
81	
82	
83	_KNOWN_TASKS = NUMERIC_TASKS | {
84	    "functional_part_grounding", "functional_object_grounding",
85	    "relative_position_forward_reasoning", "relative_depth_forward",
86	    "existence_verification", "multi_turn_qa_data",
87	}
88	
89	
90	def _task_from_path(path: Path) -> Optional[str]:
91	    for part in path.parts[::-1]:
92	        if part in _KNOWN_TASKS:
93	            return part
94	    return None
95	
96	
97	def gather_samples(input_path: Path) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
98	    files = [input_path] if input_path.is_file() else sorted(input_path.rglob("*.json"))
99	    if not files:
100	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No .json prediction files found under {input_path}")
101	    samples: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
102	    for f in files:
103	        try:
104	            data = json.load(open(f, encoding="utf-8"))
105	        except Exception as e:
106	            print(f"[WARN] skipping {f}: {e}")
107	            continue
108	        path_task = _task_from_path(f)
109	        for s in flatten_with_task(data):
110	            if not s.get("_task") or s["_task"] not in _KNOWN_TASKS:
111	                s["_task"] = path_task or s.get("_task")
112	            samples.append(s)
113	    return samples
114

116	# =========================== local LLM (transformers) ===========================
117	class LocalLLM:
118	    """One HF LM sharded across the given GPUs (device_map='auto'); deterministic (greedy) chat.
119	
120	    ``backend='causal'`` (default) loads ``AutoModelForCausalLM`` — the text model used for APE
121	    number-extraction and GM-delta. ``backend='vl'`` loads ``Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration``
122	    via ``AutoProcessor`` — the Table-4 **judge** (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct) that scores
123	    Hallucination + Completeness."""
124	
125	    def __init__(self, model_path: str, gpus: str = "", backend: str = "causal"):
126	        import torch
127	        if gpus:
128	            os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = gpus
129	        self.torch = torch
130	        self.backend = backend
131	        print(f"[LLM] loading {model_path} (transformers backend={backend}, no vLLM) ...")
132	        if backend == "vl":
133	            from transformers import AutoProcessor, Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration
134	            self.tok = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
135	            self.model = Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
136	                model_path, dtype="auto", device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True).eval()
137	        else:
138	            from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
139	            self.tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
140	            self.model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
141	                model_path, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True).eval()
142	
143	    def chat(self, system: str, user: str, max_new_tokens: int = 512) -> str:
144	        if self.backend == "vl":
145	            msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": system}]},
146	                    {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": user}]}]
147	            text = self.tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
148	            inputs = self.tok(text=[text], return_tensors="pt").to(self.model.device)
149	            with self.torch.no_grad():
150	                out = self.model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, do_sample=False)
151	            return self.tok.decode(out[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)
152	        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
153	        text = self.tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
154	        ids = self.tok(text, return_tensors="pt").to(self.model.device)
155	        with self.torch.no_grad():
156	            out = self.model.generate(**ids, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, do_sample=False,
157	                                      repetition_penalty=1.05)
158	        return self.tok.decode(out[0][ids["input_ids"].shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)
159

161	# =========================== LLM number extraction (Sec. 2) ===========================
162	EXTRACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a precise extraction assistant. You will receive a task type, a question, a ground-truth answer (gt_answer), and a predicted answer (pred_answer). Your job is to extract numerical values (in meters) according to the task type and return a single JSON object.
163	
164	TASK TYPES AND EXTRACTION RULES:
165	
166	1) distance_estimation
167	   - Extract exactly one distance in meters from each answer.
168	   - Output: {"extracted_gt": {"distance_m": <float>}, "extracted_pred": {"distance_m": <float>}}
169	   - If a value is missing in an answer, use 0.0 for that key so the metric can penalize.
170	
171	2) grounded_dimension_reasoning AND scale_estimation
172	   - Extract length_m, width_m, thickness_m (in that order: length x width x thickness) when the question asks for dimensions/size.
173	   - If the question asks only for one dimension (e.g. only thickness, only width, only length), extract only that dimension for both gt and pred.
174	   - If the question asks for distance from the camera (e.g. "how far from the camera"), also extract "distance_from_camera_m" for both answers.
175	   - Output: {"extracted_gt": {"length_m"?: float, "width_m"?: float, "thickness_m"?: float, "distance_from_camera_m"?: float}, "extracted_pred": {...}}
176	   - Use only the keys that apply to the question. If a value is present in gt but missing in pred, use 0.0 for pred.
177	
178	3) scale_comparison_size
179	   - Extract dimensions for TWO objects: object1 (first mentioned) and object2 (second mentioned).
180	   - Each object: [length_m, width_m, thickness_m] in that order.
181	   - Output: {"extracted_gt": {"object1": [l, w, t], "object2": [l, w, t]}, "extracted_pred": {"object1": [l, w, t], "object2": [l, w, t]}}
182	   - If pred does not contain numbers for an object, use [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] for that object.
183	
184	RULES:
185	- Return ONLY valid JSON. No markdown, no code fences, no explanation.
186	- All numbers in meters as floats.
187	- If gt has a value and pred does not, set the pred value to 0.0 for that key."""
188	
189	
190	def build_extraction_user(task: str, question: str, gt: str, pred: str) -> str:
191	    return (f"Task: {task}\n\nQuestion: {question}\n\ngt_answer: {gt}\n\npred_answer: {pred}\n\n"
192	            "Extract the required numbers and return a single JSON object with keys extracted_gt and "
193	            "extracted_pred as specified for this task. Output only the JSON.")
194	
195	
196	def parse_extraction(resp: str, task: str) -> Tuple[Optional[dict], Optional[dict]]:
197	    s = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\s*|\s*```$", "", (resp or "").strip(), flags=re.S).strip()
198	    blob = re.search(r"\{.*\}", s, re.S)
199	    for cand in (s, blob.group(0) if blob else None):
200	        if not cand:
201	            continue
202	        try:
203	            d = json.loads(cand)
204	            if isinstance(d, dict) and "extracted_gt" in d and "extracted_pred" in d:
205	                return d["extracted_gt"], d["extracted_pred"]
206	        except Exception:
207	            pass
208	    if task == "distance_estimation":   # regex fallback — distance only
209	        nums = re.findall(r"(\d+\.?\d*)\s*(?:m|meters?|metres?)", resp or "")
210	        if len(nums) >= 2:
211	            return {"distance_m": float(nums[0])}, {"distance_m": float(nums[1])}
212	        if len(nums) == 1:
213	            return {"distance_m": float(nums[0])}, {"distance_m": 0.0}
214	    return None, None
215	
216	
217	def fill_missing_with_zero(eg: dict, ep: dict) -> dict:
218	    ep = dict(ep or {})
219	    for k, v in (eg or {}).items():
220	        if k not in ep or ep[k] is None:
221	            ep[k] = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] if isinstance(v, list) else 0.0
222	    return ep
223

225	# =========================== APE / delta (Sec. 3) ===========================
226	def _f(x):
227	    try:
228	        return float(x)
229	    except Exception:
230	        return None
231	
232	
233	def get_pairs_for_task(task: str, eg: dict, ep: dict) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
234	    pairs: List[Tuple[float, float]] = []
235	    if task == "distance_estimation":
236	        g = _f((eg or {}).get("distance_m"))
237	        if g is not None:
238	            p = _f((ep or {}).get("distance_m", 0.0))
239	            pairs.append((g, p if p is not None else 0.0))
240	    elif task in ("grounded_dimension_reasoning", "scale_estimation"):
241	        for k, gv in (eg or {}).items():
242	            if isinstance(gv, list):
243	                continue
244	            g = _f(gv)
245	            if g is None:
246	                continue
247	            p = _f((ep or {}).get(k, 0.0))
248	            pairs.append((g, p if p is not None else 0.0))
249	    elif task == "scale_comparison_size":
250	        for obj in ("object1", "object2"):
251	            gl = (eg or {}).get(obj, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
252	            pl = (ep or {}).get(obj, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
253	            if not (isinstance(gl, list) and len(gl) == 3):
254	                gl = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
255	            if not (isinstance(pl, list) and len(pl) == 3):
256	                pl = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
257	            for i in range(3):
258	                g = _f(gl[i])
259	                if g is None:
260	                    continue
261	                p = _f(pl[i])
262	                pairs.append((g, p if p is not None else 0.0))
263	    return pairs
264	
265	
266	def ape_delta_from_pairs(pairs: List[Tuple[float, float]], tau: float = 1.25) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
267	    apes, ratios, succ = [], [], []
268	    for g, p in pairs:
269	        if g == 0:                      # GT==0 pairs are EXCLUDED (not scored)
270	            continue
271	        apes.append(abs((g - p) / g) * 100.0)
272	        r = math.inf if p == 0 else max(p / g, g / p)
273	        ratios.append(r)
274	        succ.append(1.0 if r <= tau else 0.0)
275	    if not apes:
276	        return None
277	    return {"ape_percent": round(mean(apes), 4),
278	            "delta_ratio": (math.inf if math.inf in ratios else round(mean(ratios), 4)),
279	            "delta_success": round(mean(succ), 4),
280	            "n_pairs": len(apes)}
281	
282	
283	# =========================== stage: ape ===========================
284	def stage_ape(samples, llm: "LocalLLM", tau: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
285	    from tqdm import tqdm
286	    per_task: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, float]]] = {}
287	    n_fail = 0
288	    numeric = [s for s in samples if s.get("_task") in NUMERIC_TASKS]
289	    print(f"[ape] {len(numeric)} numerical-task samples (of {len(samples)})")
290	    for s in tqdm(numeric, desc="extract+ape"):
291	        task = s["_task"]
292	        resp = llm.chat(EXTRACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
293	                        build_extraction_user(task, s.get("question", ""),
294	                                              s.get("gt_answer", ""), s.get("pred_answer", "")))
295	        eg, ep = parse_extraction(resp, task)
296	        if eg is None:
297	            n_fail += 1
298	            continue
299	        ep = fill_missing_with_zero(eg, ep)
300	        res = ape_delta_from_pairs(get_pairs_for_task(task, eg, ep), tau=tau)
301	        if res is not None:
302	            per_task.setdefault(task, []).append(res)
303	    summary: Dict[str, Any] = {"tau": tau, "extraction_failures": n_fail, "per_task": {}}
304	    all_qa: List[Dict[str, float]] = []
305	    for task, lst in per_task.items():
306	        all_qa += lst
307	        summary["per_task"][task] = {
308	            "n": len(lst),
309	            "APE_percent": round(mean(x["ape_percent"] for x in lst), 4),
310	            "delta@1.25_success_rate": round(mean(x["delta_success"] for x in lst), 4),
311	        }
312	    if all_qa:
313	        summary["overall"] = {
314	            "n": len(all_qa),
315	            "APE_percent": round(mean(x["ape_percent"] for x in all_qa), 4),
316	            "delta@1.25_success_rate": round(mean(x["delta_success"] for x in all_qa), 4),
317	        }
318	    return summary
319

321	# =========================== stage: judge (paper Table-4: Hallucination + Completeness) ===========================
322	# The Table-4 judge is Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct; it scores each prediction and reports
323	# Hallucination + Completeness.
324	JUDGE_SYSTEM = (
325	    "You are an evaluation assistant. Given a user question, a ground-truth answer, "
326	    "and a model's predicted answer, you must evaluate the prediction on several "
327	    "dimensions on a scale from 1 to 10. Return ONLY a valid JSON object with numeric "
328	    "fields and optional 'metric_accuracy_reason' and 'comments' fields."
329	)
330	
331	
332	def build_judge_user(q: str, gt: str, pred: str) -> str:
333	    return f"""Question:
334	{q}
335	
336	Ground truth answer:
337	{gt}
338	
339	Model predicted answer:
340	{pred}
341	
342	Please rate the following metrics from 1 to 10 (1 = very bad, 10 = excellent):
343	
344	- hallucination: How much the prediction contains fabricated or unsupported content
345	  (10 = no hallucination, strictly supported by GT; 1 = mostly hallucinated).
346	- accuracy: How factually correct and faithful the prediction is compared to the ground truth.
347	- completeness: How completely the prediction covers the ground truth information.
348	- reasoning_quality: How coherent and logically sound the reasoning is.
349	
350	Additionally, if there are any numeric metrics (numbers such as sizes, distances, thickness, counts, etc.)
351	in BOTH the ground truth answer and the predicted answer, you must also:
352	
353	1. Compare corresponding numbers and estimate their percentage difference.
354	2. Based on these numeric differences, assign a 'metric_accuracy' score from 1 to 10:
355	   - 10 = numbers are almost identical (e.g., average percentage difference < 5%)
356	   - 8-9 = small differences (e.g., 5% ~ 15%)
357	   - 5-7 = moderate differences (e.g., 15% ~ 40%)
358	   - 1-4 = large or very large differences (e.g., > 40% or severely incorrect)
359	3. Provide a short explanation in 'metric_accuracy_reason' summarizing the numeric differences,
360	   for example: "Predicted dimensions differ by ~18% on average from ground truth."
361	
362	If there are NO numeric metrics to compare, set:
363	- metric_accuracy = null
364	- metric_accuracy_reason = "No numeric metrics to compare."
365	
366	Return a JSON object with the following structure:
367	
368	{{
369	  "hallucination": <number between 1 and 10>,
370	  "accuracy": <number between 1 and 10>,
371	  "completeness": <number between 1 and 10>,
372	  "reasoning_quality": <number between 1 and 10>,
373	  "metric_accuracy": <number between 1 and 10, or null if no numeric metrics>,
374	  "metric_accuracy_reason": "<short numeric-difference explanation, or null>",
375	  "comments": "<optional short overall explanation>"
376	}}
377	
378	Do not include any text before or after the JSON."""
379	
380	
381	def _parse_judge_json(resp: str) -> Optional[dict]:
382	    s = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\s*|\s*```$", "", (resp or "").strip(), flags=re.S)
383	    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", s, re.S)
384	    for cand in (s, m.group(0) if m else None):
385	        if not cand:
386	            continue
387	        try:
388	            return json.loads(cand)
389	        except Exception:
390	            pass
391	    return None
392	
393	
394	def stage_judge(samples, llm: "LocalLLM") -> Dict[str, Any]:
395	    from tqdm import tqdm
396	    h_sum = c_sum = 0.0
397	    n = 0
398	    for s in tqdm(samples, desc="judge"):
399	        d = _parse_judge_json(llm.chat(
400	            JUDGE_SYSTEM,
401	            build_judge_user(s.get("question", ""), s.get("gt_answer", ""), s.get("pred_answer", "")),
402	            max_new_tokens=512))
403	        if d:
404	            # keep the Hallucination + Completeness scores from the judge's JSON
405	            hv, cv = d.get("hallucination"), d.get("completeness")
406	            if isinstance(hv, (int, float)) and isinstance(cv, (int, float)):
407	                h_sum += float(hv)
408	                c_sum += float(cv)
409	                n += 1
410	    if n == 0:
411	        return {"n_judged": 0}
412	    return {"hallucination": round(h_sum / n, 4), "completeness": round(c_sum / n, 4), "n_judged": n}
413	
414	
415	# =========================== stage: GM-delta (paper, supplementary) ===========================
416	def _mask_iou(gt, pred) -> Optional[float]:
417	    """Mean instance IoU for one QA's masks (gt/pred each [n_obj, N] bool), matching the seg metric."""
418	    import numpy as np
419	
420	    def to2d(m):
421	        m = np.asarray(m, dtype=object) if isinstance(m, list) else np.asarray(m)
422	        if m.dtype == object:
423	            m = np.stack([np.asarray(r) for r in m]) if m.ndim else np.asarray(m.item())
424	        m = np.asarray(m)
425	        return m[None, :] if m.ndim == 1 else m
426	
427	    g, p = to2d(gt).astype(bool), to2d(pred).astype(bool)
428	    k = min(g.shape[0], p.shape[0])
429	    if k == 0:
430	        return None
431	    g, p = g[:k], p[:k]
432	    valid = g.sum(-1) > 0
433	    if valid.sum() == 0:
434	        return None
435	    ious = (g & p).sum(-1) / ((g | p).sum(-1) + 1e-8)
436	    return float(ious[valid].mean())
437	
438	
439	def stage_gmdelta(input_path: Path, mask_dump_dir: Path, llm: "LocalLLM",
440	                  tasks, iou_thr: float = 0.3, tau: float = 1.25) -> Dict[str, Any]:
441	    """GM-delta (Grounded-Measurement): a prediction succeeds iff **mask IoU > iou_thr AND numeric
442	    delta <= tau**. **Auto-discovers** every ``<dataset>/.../<numeric task>/`` prediction directory
443	    under ``--input`` (both ScanNet and ScanNet++), lines each up with the mirrored per-QA mask dump
444	    under ``--mask_dump_dir`` (produced by a Step-1 run with ``--mask-dump``), and reports GM-delta
445	    **per (dataset, task) + overall**. ``tasks`` = set of sub-tasks to include (e.g. the 4 numeric)."""
446	    import numpy as np
447	    from collections import defaultdict
448	    from tqdm import tqdm
449	    pred_files = [input_path] if input_path.is_file() else sorted(input_path.rglob("*.json"))
450	    base = input_path if input_path.is_dir() else input_path.parent
451	    groups: Dict[Path, List[Path]] = defaultdict(list)
452	    for pf in pred_files:
453	        groups[pf.parent].append(pf)
454	
455	    per_group: Dict[str, Any] = {}
456	    tot = {"n": 0, "succ": 0, "iou_ok": 0, "delta_ok": 0}
457	    for tdir in sorted(groups, key=str):
458	        task = tdir.name
459	        if task not in tasks:                      # only the requested (numeric) tasks
460	            continue
461	        try:
462	            rel = tdir.relative_to(base)
463	        except ValueError:
464	            rel = Path(".")
465	        mdir = mask_dump_dir / rel                 # mirror of the prediction tree
466	        ds = next((p for p in tdir.parts if p in ("scannet", "scannetpp")), "data")
467	        g = {"n": 0, "succ": 0, "iou_ok": 0, "delta_ok": 0}
468	        for pf in tqdm(groups[tdir], desc=f"gm-δ {ds}/{task}", leave=False):
469	            mp, mg = mdir / f"{pf.stem}_qa_pred_masks.npy", mdir / f"{pf.stem}_qa_gt_masks.npy"
470	            if not (mp.exists() and mg.exists()):
471	                continue
472	            samples = [s for s in flatten_with_task(json.load(open(pf, encoding="utf-8")))
473	                       if s.get("_task") in (task, None)]
474	            pred_masks, gt_masks = list(np.load(mp, allow_pickle=True)), list(np.load(mg, allow_pickle=True))
475	            for i, s in enumerate(samples):
476	                if i >= len(pred_masks) or i >= len(gt_masks):
477	                    break
478	                iou = _mask_iou(gt_masks[i], pred_masks[i])
479	                if iou is None:
480	                    continue
481	                eg, ep = parse_extraction(
482	                    llm.chat(EXTRACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
483	                             build_extraction_user(task, s.get("question", ""),
484	                                                   s.get("gt_answer", ""), s.get("pred_answer", ""))), task)
485	                res = (ape_delta_from_pairs(get_pairs_for_task(task, eg, fill_missing_with_zero(eg, ep)), tau=tau)
486	                       if eg is not None else None)
487	                delta_ok = (res is not None and res["delta_success"] >= 1.0)
488	                iou_ok = iou > iou_thr
489	                g["n"] += 1
490	                g["iou_ok"] += int(iou_ok)
491	                g["delta_ok"] += int(delta_ok)
492	                g["succ"] += int(iou_ok and delta_ok)
493	        if g["n"]:
494	            per_group[f"{ds}/{task}"] = {
495	                "n": g["n"],
496	                "GM_delta_success_rate": round(g["succ"] / g["n"], 4),
497	                "mask_iou>thr_rate": round(g["iou_ok"] / g["n"], 4),
498	                "delta<=tau_rate": round(g["delta_ok"] / g["n"], 4)}
499	            for k in tot:
500	                tot[k] += g[k]
501	    out: Dict[str, Any] = {"iou_thr": iou_thr, "tau": tau, "per_group": per_group}
502	    if tot["n"]:
503	        out["overall"] = {"n": tot["n"], "GM_delta_success_rate": round(tot["succ"] / tot["n"], 4)}
504	    else:
505	        out["error"] = ("no joined (scene, task) groups — run the numeric sub-tasks with --mask-dump, "
506	                        "then point --input at the prediction root and --mask_dump_dir at the mask root")
507	    return out
508	
509	
510	# =========================== self-test (reference fixtures T1-T4) ===========================
511	def selftest() -> int:
512	    cases = [
513	        ("distance_estimation", {"distance_m": 0.899}, {"distance_m": 3.5}, 289.3215, 3.8932, 0.0),
514	        ("grounded_dimension_reasoning", {"length_m": 1.78, "width_m": 0.78, "thickness_m": 0.53},
515	         {"length_m": 2.1, "width_m": 0.9, "thickness_m": 0.7}, 21.8125, 1.2181, 0.6667),
516	        ("scale_estimation", {"length_m": 1.78, "width_m": 0.78, "thickness_m": 0.53},
517	         {"length_m": 2.0, "width_m": 0.8, "thickness_m": 0.7}, 15.6664, 1.1567, 0.6667),
518	        ("scale_comparison_size", {"object1": [0.13, 0.09, 0.05], "object2": [0.61, 0.51, 0.09]},
519	         {"object1": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "object2": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]}, 100.0, math.inf, 0.0),
520	    ]
521	    ok = True
522	    for task, eg, ep, ape_e, ratio_e, succ_e in cases:
523	        r = ape_delta_from_pairs(get_pairs_for_task(task, eg, ep))
524	        pa = abs(r["ape_percent"] - ape_e) < 1e-2
525	        pr = (r["delta_ratio"] == math.inf) if ratio_e == math.inf else abs(r["delta_ratio"] - ratio_e) < 1e-2
526	        ps = abs(r["delta_success"] - succ_e) < 1e-3
527	        ok &= pa and pr and ps
528	        print(f"  {task:30} ape={r['ape_percent']:<10} delta={r['delta_ratio']:<8} "
529	              f"succ={r['delta_success']}  -> {'OK' if (pa and pr and ps) else 'FAIL'}")
530	    print("SELFTEST:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
531	    return 0 if ok else 1
532

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.
